prompt:
Which of these pairs of results, taken together, prove p if and only if q? Select all that apply.

*Symbols: ¬ means NOT; → means "implies" (if ... then); ↔ means "if and only if".*

options.text: p implies q and q implies p
options.explanation: Correct. This is the definition of the biconditional: both directions.

options.text: p implies q and not q implies not p
options.explanation: not q implies not p is the contrapositive of p implies q, so this proves the same direction twice and never shows q implies p.

options.text: p implies q and not p implies not q
options.explanation: Correct. not p implies not q is the contrapositive of q implies p, so this covers both directions.

options.text: not q implies not p and not p implies not q
options.explanation: Correct. These are the contrapositives of p implies q and q implies p respectively.

workedExample: An if-and-only-if claim needs both directions. A supplies them directly. C supplies the forward implication and the contrapositive of the reverse; D supplies both contrapositives. B proves the forward direction twice and never establishes the reverse.

prompt: Every integer square leaves remainder zero or one when divided by four. A target leaves remainder three. What can you conclude about representing it as a sum of two integer squares?

options.text: A larger search is required before any conclusion
options.explanation: The exhaustive remainder cases already cover all integer pairs.
Correct. The possible remainder sums are zero, one or two, never three.

options.text: A representation exists because both remainders can be odd
options.explanation: Two odd-square remainders add to two, not three.

options.text: Every target with remainder zero, one or two has a representation
options.explanation: The test gives a necessary condition only, not a sufficient one.

workedExample: Every square leaves remainder zero or one. Adding any two of those remainders gives zero, one or two, never three. This rules out a target with remainder three. It does not prove that every target with an allowed remainder has a representation.
